title: On Devoting a whole winter to the book
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：devote　|　正文 353 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 devote 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the postman ① devoted a whole winter to the book twice over, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the postman ② devotes a whole winter to the book year after year without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ devote a whole winter to the book at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ devoted a whole winter to the book before — a line in the list for June 1959 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Devoting a whole winter to the book twice over, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ devote two rooms to the children year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Devote two rooms to the children at once and never mention it again.

By 1972 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new sender from the next office ⑧ devotes two rooms to the children twice over every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the box, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ devoted a whole winter to the book again when nobody else would.

⑩ To devote a whole winter to the book, my mother said in 1977, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody devotes a whole winter to the book year after year again and somebody must devote a whole winter to the book twice over all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 献出（一般过去式 devoted a whole winter to the book：1965 年邮差头一回这样做，来回两遍）
B. v. 献出（一般现在 devotes a whole winter to the book：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 献出（不定式 to devote a whole winter to the book：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 献出（过去完成时 had devoted a whole winter to the book：1959 年六月的收发清单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 献出（动名词 devoting a whole winter to the book 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 专用（devote two rooms to the children：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去专用把两间屋专给孩子们）
G. v. 专用（devote two rooms to the children：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 献出（后段两处：新来的寄信人照例 devotes two rooms to the children，而母亲又一次 devoted a whole winter to the book）

answers.why: devote 意为“献出”，1965 年邮差来回两遍献出把一整个冬天扑在那本书上，那是邮局里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 devoted。
devote 意为“献出”，自那以后邮差年年地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 devotes。
devote 意为“献出”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯献出把一整个冬天扑在那本书上”，此处为不定式 to devote a whole winter to the book。
devote 意为“献出”，收发清单里 六月 那行字说明早在 1972 年之前就有人献出过，故用过去完成时 had devoted。
devote 意为“献出”，邮差说“献出把一整个冬天扑在那本书上这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 devoting a whole winter to the book 作主语。
devote 意为“专用”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去专用把两间屋专给孩子们”，should ever 之后用原形 devote two rooms to the children。
devote 意为“专用”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻专用把两间屋专给孩子们（devote two rooms to the children at once），以后再也不要提起。
devote 意为“献出”，新来的寄信人每个星期都照例专用把两间屋专给孩子们，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 devotes。
devote 意为“献出”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次来回两遍献出把一整个冬天扑在那本书上，用一般过去式 devoted 叙述。
devote 意为“献出”，结尾那句是母亲 1977 年的话：要献出把一整个冬天扑在那本书上，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和邮局记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1965 年，邮差来回两遍献出把一整个冬天扑在那本书上；邮局里每一个寄信人都说这是头一回。（devoted a whole winter to the book）
多年以后，邮差仍年年地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（devotes a whole winter to the book）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯献出把一整个冬天扑在那本书上这件事本身。（to devote a whole winter to the book）
早在 1959 年就有人献出把一整个冬天扑在那本书上，六月那天收发清单上的一行字就是证据。（had devoted a whole winter to the book）
邮差说过，来回两遍献出把一整个冬天扑在那本书上这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（devoting a whole winter to the book 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻专用把两间屋专给孩子们，以后再也不要提起。（devote two rooms to the children，祈使句）
answers: In 1965 the postman devoted a whole winter to the book twice over, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three weeks on, the postman still devotes a whole winter to the book year after year without being asked.
My mother said later that to devote a whole winter to the book at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had devoted a whole winter to the book long before 1972, and the line in the list for June proves it.
Devoting a whole winter to the book twice over, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
The rule the old hands handed down was plain: Devote two rooms to the children at once and never mention it again.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 devote 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1965 the postman devoted a whole winter to the book twice over, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the postman devotes a whole winter to the book year after year whenever the office asks.
Devoting a whole winter to the book twice over, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever devote two rooms to the children year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sender from the next office devotes two rooms to the children twice over every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother devoted a whole winter to the book again, and the office remembered that half.
